answer.rationale: The 18% spend reduction mandate and 14-day renewal deadline create pressure, but the 94% volume utilization leaves no buffer for switching risk. Verifying memory_c6 (multi-year pricing leverage) and memory_c2 (switching feasibility and speed) informs whether aggressive renegotiation can meet the cost target without migration risk. memory_c4 shows benchmarking recovered real margin at renewal. Negotiating_terms preserves the incumbent relationship while pursuing the cost reduction, avoiding the delivery risk of a switch when utilization is tight. If negotiation fails within 7 days, deferral to month-to-month becomes the backstop, maintaining supply continuity. This approach directly addresses the primary objective: cost reduction without increasing delivery risk. The assembly line buffer constraint is the binding constraint here.
